assessment.nobel_worthiness: Heterobifunctional degraders and molecular glues convert protein binding into catalytic removal of the target, a conceptually original shift from inhibition that widens the druggable proteome. The chemistry of linkers, E3 ligands and ternary complexes is highly design-driven, and many degraders are in clinical trials.
assessment.attribution: Crews and Deshaies introduced the first PROTAC concept; Ciulli supplied the VHL ligands and ternary-complex structural rationale. The thalidomide/cereblon mechanism (Handa, Ito, Sakamoto, Kim, Gray) is a parallel, partly separate line, so a three-person split leaves real credit unresolved.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of work, with multiple independent labs and industry programs and clinical readouts. Timing is good, though approved degrader drugs are still few.
uncertainties: Allocation between the PROTAC lineage and the cereblon/molecular-glue lineage is contested.
Clinical proof of broad therapeutic benefit is still emerging.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Ionizable lipid nanoparticles are the enabling chemistry for siRNA and mRNA medicines, solving encapsulation, endosomal escape and tolerability through lipid pKa design. Their societal impact through mRNA vaccines is exceptional and clearly chemical in character.
assessment.attribution: Cullis and Madden developed the core ionizable-lipid LNP formulation, and Anderson and Langer drove lipidoid discovery and screening. Credit among Cullis, Hope, MacLachlan, Madden, Anderson and Langer is spread, and the mRNA vaccine prize to Kariko and Weissman complicates the narrative.
assessment.maturity: Clinically validated at global scale with Onpattro and mRNA vaccines, and the confirmation is independent and robust. Recognition is timely.
uncertainties: Overlap with the 2023 Physiology or Medicine prize may weigh on committee appetite.
Which lipid design contributions are decisive is debated.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Quantitative, large-scale proteomics by mass spectrometry turned protein identification into a systems-level measurement. The analytical and methodological advances (shotgun, SRM/targeted, quantitation) underpin modern biology and clinical biomarker work.
assessment.attribution: Mann, Aebersold and Yates are the most natural trio, covering high-resolution quantitative proteomics, targeted/SRM and proteome-wide approaches. Hunt, Gygi and Heck also have strong claims, so the cutoff is difficult.
assessment.maturity: Mature and widely adopted for more than 20 years. Ionization (Fenn, Tanaka) was already recognized, so this is a natural continuation.
uncertainties: Crowded credit field makes a fair three-person split contentious.
Possible view that the method is an extension of the already-recognized ionization breakthrough.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Liquid-liquid phase separation reframed how cells compartmentalize biochemistry without membranes, linking soft-matter physics with molecular biology and disease. It is conceptually original and has broad influence, and designed-peptide and protein-domain work relies on its principles.
assessment.attribution: Hyman and Brangwynne showed P granules as liquid droplets, and Rosen showed multivalent-domain phase separation in vitro. Pappu and Mittag contributed the physical-chemical framework for sequence grammar.
assessment.maturity: Rapidly growing and highly cited, but the physiological relevance and the boundaries of the condensate concept remain debated. Possibly slightly early.
uncertainties: Debate over which condensates are truly liquid and functionally relevant in vivo.
Fit with the chemistry prize versus physiology or medicine is uncertain.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Halide perovskites reached silicon-competitive solar-cell efficiencies within roughly a decade, a striking materials-chemistry advance in composition, defect and interface control.
assessment.attribution: Miyasaka reported the first perovskite-sensitized cells, Snaith demonstrated the efficient solid-state device, and Park produced the first solid-state cell with stability. Grätzel, Seok and Kanatzidis also have credible claims, so credit is crowded.
assessment.maturity: Efficiency gains are confirmed by many labs, but long-term stability, lead toxicity and commercial scale-up are unresolved, which argues for waiting.
uncertainties: Device stability and commercial viability are unproven.
Allocation among six credited names is contested.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Orthogonal tRNA/synthetase pairs for incorporating noncanonical amino acids give chemists site-specific control of protein chemistry in living cells. This is directly relevant to engineered peptides and proteins and to biomaterial and biosensor design.
assessment.attribution: Schultz and Wang opened the field in E. coli and then in eukaryotic cells, and Chin extended it to multiple codons and orthogonal ribosomes. Mehl and Yokoyama contributed but are likely secondary.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of independent confirmation and widespread use, and the technology is mature. Applications are widespread in research and growing in therapeutics.
uncertainties: Division of credit between Schultz and his former group members is a sensitivity.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Programming nanoparticle assembly with DNA, and spherical nucleic acids, created a chemically precise route to nanostructured materials and plasmonic diagnostics, and enabled colorimetric biosensors and intracellular gene regulation. The ideas are original and clearly chemical.
assessment.attribution: Mirkin and Alivisatos published the founding 1996 papers on DNA-nanoparticle assembly independently, and Mirkin went on to develop spherical nucleic acids. Storhoff and Mucic are early coauthors, but a two-person prize is most defensible.
assessment.maturity: Established for about 30 years with diagnostics on the market, though clinical impact of spherical nucleic acid therapeutics is still modest.
uncertainties: Alivisatos may be considered more for quantum dots than for this line.
Therapeutic validation of spherical nucleic acids is limited.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Native chemical ligation lets chemists assemble proteins from synthetic and recombinant fragments, giving access to modified, labeled or unnatural proteins and extending chemical synthesis to protein scale. It has strong relevance to peptide design and engineering.
assessment.attribution: Kent and Dawson reported native chemical ligation, and Muir developed expressed protein ligation, which brought it to biologists. Danishefsky, Brik and Liu are other significant contributors.
assessment.maturity: Mature and validated by 30 years of use, so recognition would be timely.
uncertainties: The boundary between ligation chemistry and its later applications.
Impact is concentrated in specialist chemical biology, less visible to a general audience.
